questions.scenario: It's Diwali and time for the ultimate 'Ghar ki Safai' and decoration. What is your main job?

options.text: Climbing the ladder, hammering the nails, and physically hanging the heavy flower torans and fairy lights.
Making sure the heavy brass diyas and thalis are placed perfectly so the glass center table doesn't crack.
Planning the exact color combination of the rangoli and deciding which curtains match the new sofa covers.
Managing the budget given by Mummy to buy the best lights, sweets, and gifts without running out of cash.

questions.scenario: Your family is shifting to a new rented flat. What is your top priority during the move?

options.text: Helping the packers lift the heavy cartons and directing them exactly where to drop the fridge and washing machine.
Using an inch-tape to measure the doorways to ensure the massive wooden double bed will actually fit through.
Visualizing where the TV should go so the natural sunlight from the balcony hits the living room perfectly.
Checking how close the society is to the Metro station, local market, and your tuition classes.

questions.scenario: You are playing a world-building game like Minecraft with your friends. What is your play style?

options.text: Mining resources endlessly and doing the hard physical labor to build the giant outer walls quickly.
Calculating the exact symmetry of the foundation so your mega-fortress is perfectly balanced and won't collapse.
Focusing on the aesthetics—adding indoor waterfalls, glass windows, and cool torches to set the vibe.
Building a massive village with a trading market and charging your friends resources to live in your city.

questions.scenario: It's the inter-school Science Exhibition and your group is making a working model. What's your role?

options.text: Cutting the thick cardboard, hot-gluing the PVC pipes, and doing the messy, hands-on assembly.
Calculating the exact battery voltage or water pressure needed to make sure the moving parts don't break.
Painting the model beautifully and designing a stunning presentation chart with flawless handwriting.
Organizing the team, dividing the tasks, and making sure the project is completed within the Rs. 500 collected fund.

questions.scenario: You are on a family trip to Goa or Puri, building a massive sandcastle on the beach. What is your approach?

options.text: Digging the deep moat with your bare hands, packing the wet sand hard, and piling up the tallest towers.
Mixing the exact ratio of wet and dry sand so the heavy walls can stand up against the ocean breeze.
Using a stick and shells to carve beautiful, intricate doors, windows, and balconies into the sand walls.
Scouting the perfect, flat spot away from the high-tide waves so your masterpiece survives the longest.

questions.scenario: Papa sits on a wooden dining chair and its leg breaks. How do you respond?

options.text: Grab the hammer, nails, and Fevicol from the toolbox to practically fix it right then and there.
Analyze the angle of the break and figure out where the center of gravity failed to prevent it from happening again.
Tell Papa it's a sign to finally throw it away and buy a stylish, modern set of chairs that match the dining table.
Calculate if paying a carpenter Rs. 300 to fix it is a better deal than buying a new plastic chair for Rs. 500.

questions.scenario: You are hanging out at a massive, swanky new shopping mall in the city. What catches your eye?

options.text: Looking at the massive concrete pillars in the basement parking and wondering how they were poured.
Staring at the giant glass dome ceiling and trying to figure out how the steel frame supports all that weight.
Admiring the beautiful luxury store displays, the premium floor tiles, and the warm yellow lighting.
Thinking about how much rent the big anchor stores (like Lifestyle or PVR) must be paying every month.

questions.scenario: During a tense game of Gully Cricket, a dispute breaks out over the pitch boundaries. What do you do?

options.text: Take a brick or chalk and physically draw thick, clear crease and boundary lines on the road yourself.
Argue that the road is slightly sloped on one side, making the bounce totally unfair for the fast bowlers.
Complain that the pitch area is full of garbage and clear out a neat, clean patch so the game feels better.
Negotiate with the kids from the neighboring society to merge both grounds and host a massive mega-tournament.

questions.scenario: Mummy orders you and your sibling to clean and reorganize your shared bedroom. What is your strategy?

options.text: Using your physical strength to push the heavy iron almirah and study table to the other side of the room.
Checking if the flimsy wooden bookshelf can actually handle the weight of 50 new RD Sharma guidebooks.
Putting up cool posters, adding LED strip lights, and making the room look totally Pinterest-worthy.
Drawing a strict, invisible border to divide the room 50-50 so your sibling doesn't encroach on your territory.

questions.scenario: You are randomly scrolling through Instagram Reels or YouTube Shorts. Which video makes you stop and watch?

options.text: Oddly satisfying videos of workers perfectly plastering a brick wall or heavy JCB machines digging.
Documentaries breaking down the insane physics of how mega-dams or the Burj Khalifa were built.
'Before & After' extreme bedroom makeovers, DIY decor, and beautiful aesthetic home tours.
Videos like 'Why property prices in Mumbai are crazy' or 'How the layout of Chandigarh was planned'.

Site_Engineer.title: The Ground Warrior (Construction / Site Engineer)
Site_Engineer.primary_match_text: You are a hands-on, action-oriented person. You don't like sitting at a desk all day; you prefer being on the ground, wearing a hard hat, and turning blueprints into real, physical structures.
Site_Engineer.day_in_the_life: Managing massive construction sites, shouting over the noise of cement mixers, ensuring safety protocols, and leading a team of workers to build highways, bridges, or skyscrapers.
Site_Engineer.alternative_match_text: If not civil engineering, your hands-on practical skills would make you a great Mechanical Engineer, Defense Officer, or Operations Manager.
Site_Engineer.roadmap: 11th/12th: Science (PCM is mandatory). Entrance: Crack JEE Main, Advanced, or State CETs (like MHT-CET, KCET). Degree: 4-year B.Tech in Civil Engineering. Next Steps: Gain on-site internships with big construction firms like L&T.

Structural_Engineer.title: The Physics Pro (Structural Engineer)
Structural_Engineer.primary_match_text: You have a highly analytical brain. You love math, physics, and figuring out how things balance. You are the hidden genius who makes sure massive buildings don't collapse.
Structural_Engineer.day_in_the_life: Sitting with advanced software, calculating wind loads, earthquake resistance, and the exact thickness of steel rods needed for a 50-story building.
Structural_Engineer.alternative_match_text: Your love for calculations and physics makes you a perfect fit for Aerospace Engineering, Data Science, or Applied Mathematics.
Structural_Engineer.roadmap: 11th/12th: Science (PCM is mandatory). Entrance: Crack JEE Main & Advanced. Degree: B.Tech in Civil Engineering. Next Steps: Highly recommended to pursue an M.Tech in Structural Engineering from an IIT or NIT.

Architect.title: The Space Artist (Architect / Interior Designer)
Architect.primary_match_text: You are creative, visual, and have an amazing sense of aesthetics. You care about how a space makes people feel, focusing on colors, lighting, and beautiful design.
Architect.day_in_the_life: Sketching 3D models of luxury villas, choosing premium marble flooring, designing smart-homes, and making sure a building looks like a masterpiece.
Architect.alternative_match_text: If not architecture, your visual creativity would make you a brilliant Graphic Designer, UI/UX Designer, or Fashion Designer.
Architect.roadmap: 11th/12th: Science (PCM is usually required, though some colleges allow other streams with Math). Entrance: Crack NATA (National Aptitude Test in Architecture) or JEE Main Paper-2. Degree: 5-year B.Arch (Bachelor of Architecture).

Real_Estate_Developer.title: The City Boss (Real Estate Developer / Urban Planner)
Real_Estate_Developer.primary_match_text: You are a big-picture thinker. You understand the value of things, love managing money, and have a mind for business, negotiation, and city-scale planning.
Real_Estate_Developer.day_in_the_life: Buying massive plots of land, pitching mega-township ideas to investors, tracking the stock market, and deciding where the city's next big mall should be built.
Real_Estate_Developer.alternative_match_text: Your business mindset and negotiation skills would make you an excellent Investment Banker, Entrepreneur, or Corporate Lawyer.
Real_Estate_Developer.roadmap: 11th/12th: Commerce or Arts (Math is a big advantage). Degree: BBA, B.Com, or Bachelor of Planning (B.Plan). Next Steps: Pursue an MBA in Real Estate Management or a Master's in Urban Planning.
